summary.text: Father of the Phrygian captains Phorcys (`phorcys-phrygian`) and Ascanius (`ascanius-phrygian`) from far-off Ascania — attested by Apollodorus in the catalogue of Trojan allies, while Homer names the sons but not their sire.

story.text: Homer's Catalogue sets Phorcys and godlike Ascanius at the head of the Phrygians who came from Ascania, eager to fight in the press of battle beside Troy — but the poet does not name their father in the muster.

Apollodorus, listing the allies who joined the Trojans, makes Phorcys and Ascanius sons of Aretaon among the Phrygian captains — a parentage that stands beside Homer's later naming of Phorcys as son of Phaenops in the fight over Patroclus (`phorcys-phrygian-parentage`).
